title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple
summary: Learn how to choose between the past simple and present perfect tenses. You will be able to talk about your life experiences and finished past actions easily.

sections.p: Use the past simple when you talk about an action that happened at a specific time in the past. The time is usually mentioned, like yesterday, last week, or in 2010. The action is completely finished, and we care more about when it happened than the result today.

ex.mean: The trip happened at a specific time in the past and is finished.

ex.en: She bought a new car yesterday.
ex.mean: The action happened at a known time in the past.

sections.p: Use the present perfect to talk about experiences in your life without saying exactly when they happened. We use have or has plus a past participle verb. The exact time is not important, but the experience is important for you right now.

ex.en: I have visited Paris three times.
ex.mean: This is a life experience up to now, the exact dates do not matter.
A past action that has a connection to the present moment.

sections.p: Certain words can help you choose the right tense. Words like yesterday, ago, and last point to the past simple. Words like ever, never, already, yet, just, since, and for usually point to the present perfect because they connect the past to now.

ex.mean: Asking about any time in your life up to the present moment.

ex.en: I haven't finished my homework yet.
ex.mean: An action that is not complete up to this exact moment.

tip: Ask yourself: 'Do I care when it happened?' If yes, use past simple. If you only care that it happened in your life, use present perfect.

quiz.en: She ___ never seen snow in her life.
They ___ a great movie last night.
Which sentence is correct for an unfinished action up to now?
He ___ lived in this city for five years.
